properties.name: Orientation says what is DELIVERED, and a lint keeps every report reachable
properties.rationale:
🛑 THE CHECK WAS WRITTEN FIRST AND OBSERVED FAILING, against the unfixed tree, exit 1: `named in NO skill: ['consumption_report', 'flow_report', 'ility_report', 'maturity_report', 'readiness_report', 'release_report']`. Six of fourteen. That sentence is the only evidence the failing-first step happened, which is why it is here rather than implied.

WHY THE RULE IS `*_report` AND NOT A LIST OF "EVALUATIVE" TOOLS. A hand-kept list of which tools matter is the thing that rots — the same defect this session found in `node_ref` this morning, where a judgement made once for one property was never recorded for any other. A suffix already used consistently in the code needs no maintenance and cannot silently omit a new report.

THE REGISTER CARRIES TWO KINDS OF ENTRY AND SAYS WHICH. "needs no skill" is settled; "GAP:" is a routing hole recorded rather than papered over. A test enforces the prefix, because a gap that reads as settled never gets fixed — and the cheap way to pass this check would have been to name every orphan report in whatever skill was nearest, which would satisfy the lint and defeat its purpose.

⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX. Naming was measured; INVOCATION was not. A report named in a skill is reachable, not necessarily read — and the 93-session skill-adoption result says what predicts use is an always-injected surface, which a skill is not. So this closes the "unreachable" half and leaves the "unread" half open, and the two must not be confused. The honest test of whether it worked is whether a later session, asked "is my project doing what it is supposed to do", answers with a delivery number instead of a defect count.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
Fixes `fact:the-instruction-surface-routes-to-hygiene-and-not-to-whether-the-thing-works` on both the instance and the class.

THE INSTANCE — `where-am-i` now has a step 3, "How much of it is actually working", leading with the delivery line from `graph_report_markdown` and saying what it means: something satisfies each requirement, the capability is built, its check passes, computed from the thread rather than read off a status field. It says out loud that this is usually the question the user came with, and that a report which only ever lists debt reads as a hygiene tool whatever else it can do. It also BOUNDS the number in the same breath — it measures the design's own chain, not the running system.

THE CLASS — `skill_lint.py` gained the mirror of its oldest check. It already walked skills → tools ("every referenced tool exists"); nothing walked tools → skills, so a report could be built, correct, verified and reachable by nobody with every gate green. Now every served `*_report` must be named in some skill or carry a written reason in `UNROUTED_REPORTS`.

ROUTED, each into the skill whose job it serves rather than wherever it fit: `maturity_report` → where-am-i (the trajectory behind the snapshot), `readiness_report` → plan-increments (a GATED_ON rung decides what can ship when), `ility_report` → check-health (it reads the same sweep and says what the defects MEAN), `consumption_report` → retire-from-design (what nothing consumes is where retirement candidates come from, and its refusal to answer is itself the finding).

EXEMPTED WITH REASONS, and the two are different: `release_report` "needs no skill" — cutting a release is a repo procedure, not a design-loop step. `flow_report` is a "GAP:" — nothing owns inspecting an existing Flow; capture-intent and adopt CREATE flows and no skill reads one back. Naming it in capture-intent would have been inventing a use to satisfy the check, which is the failure the check exists to find one level up.
